body.x: JENLiFE (CEO Jinwoo Oh) announced that it will participate in CES 2026, to be held in Las Vegas from January 6 to 9, and will also compete for the CES Innovation Awards.

Held annually in January, CES is one of the world’s three largest IT exhibitions, drawing global attention as a mega-event that showcases the latest products, technologies, and trends from companies of all sizes. The Consumer Technology Association (CTA), organizer of CES, reviews global submissions for the CES Innovation Awards ahead of the event. Only about 10 percent of applicants are typically selected, and less than 1 percent go on to win the Best Innovation Award, making it one of the most competitive recognitions in the industry. Winning companies gain immediate international attention and access to a wide range of business opportunities.

Against this backdrop, JENLiFE, a functional biomaterials startup specializing in electronic noses, aims to showcase its M13 bacteriophage–based technology at CES 2026. Unlike conventional gas sensor combinations with limited detection, JENLiFE’s approach uses phage display technology to create peptide receptors on M13 bacteriophages, mimicking human olfactory receptors. This enables the electronic nose to bind to and identify odor molecules with high precision and selectivity.

By arranging multiple bacteriophages on sensors, JENLiFE builds a bio-receptor library capable of detecting more than 800 odor molecules. The company emphasizes that this method ensures both high sensitivity and reproducibility, as identical bacteriophages can be replicated with consistent performance. Beyond detection, JENLiFE plans to present its vision of “olfactory intelligence” at CES 2026, where odor data can be analyzed and predicted for diverse applications.

The healthcare sector is expected to benefit significantly. Breath and body odor analysis could enable non-invasive early detection of diseases such as lung cancer, diabetes, and oral disorders. This aligns with global trends in preventive and patient-friendly healthcare. JENLiFE also sees opportunities in air purification systems that automatically adapt to air quality, food safety monitoring that detects spoilage levels, disaster response robots that identify survivors or chemical leaks, and metaverse environments that replicate scent for heightened realism. The company is already collaborating with businesses in consumer electronics, food, and automotive industries to translate the potential of its electronic nose platform into practical solutions.

At CES 2026, JENLiFE plans to demonstrate the technology live, showcasing its real-world performance to industry experts, buyers, investors, and media. JENLiFE sees this as a springboard into the U.S. and global markets, with particular focus on healthcare, food safety, environmental monitoring, and robotics.

A company spokesperson said, “We will showcase how our M13 bacteriophage-based electronic nose platform works in practice. Through this, we aim to directly convey its strengths and applications to experts and potential partners, and actively seek collaborations and investment opportunities.” The spokesperson added, “By leveraging market insights and networks gained on-site, we intend to establish a foothold for entry into the U.S. and other global markets. We will move quickly to form partnerships with local bio, electronics, and robotics companies and institutions, while continuing networking and pilot projects beyond CES.”

At CES 2025 earlier this year, Korean startups made a strong showing, winning seven of the 19 Best Innovation Awards and securing nearly half of all Innovation Award selections. JENLiFE aims to follow in these footsteps at CES 2026 with its groundbreaking “smelling electronic nose” technology.
